To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the angular distribution (i.e., the directionality) of the output radiation in an unstable telescoped resonator depends on the nature of the nonlinear interaction of the laser radiation with the active medium.
the angular distribution of output radiation in unstable resonators is affected by nonlinearity of a fast-flow medium.
the nonlinearities in the active medium have a significant effect on the output radiation characteristics in unstable telescopic resonant cavities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to the numerical modeling of unstable telescopic optical resonators.
the development of a numerical model of an unstable resonator that allows us to take into account the diffraction of the irradiation field and the saturation of the gain in the active medium.
the development of numerical methods for solving the parabolic equation describing the interaction between an active medium and the radiation field in an unstable resonator.

the nonlinea rity of an active medium does not affect the directionality of the output radiation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonlinear properties of the active medium have a strong effect on the output beam characteristics of the unstable resonator.
the directionality of the laser beam is determined by the nature of the gain saturation of the active medium.
the angular distribution of laser radiation from unstable telescopic resonations is determined by the nature of the active medium nonlinearity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a two-level model of the active medium with homogeneous gain saturation is not suitable for describing fast-flow lasers.
the angular distribution of laser radiation is determined by the nature of the active medium and by the parameters of the unstable resonator.
